title: Pre-revocation native pairing token can recreate a device during credential purge
description: An unexpired native pairing token remains authorized across the credential-purge sequence. Native registration validates the signed token and resolves ownerID from the old subscriber index, then later consumes the nonce and persists a new device. Admin password reset, MFA clear, and deactivation delete existing devices first and rotate the subscriber ID only afterward. A concurrent registration can therefore resolve the owner before rotation, continue after device deletion, and persist a fresh device using a new attacker-chosen device ID. MFA clear leaves the account active, so the new device immediately authenticates to withMailAuth routes; deactivation leaves the device stored for later reactivation.
root_cause: handleNotificationNativeRegister in backend/internal/api/server_notifications.go does not revalidate the subscriber generation or account state before committing the device, allowing a pairing token that raced credential revocation to recreate access after the purge.
intended_behavior: Admin password reset, MFA clear, and deactivation are account-recovery/offboarding controls intended to revoke every existing and outstanding native-device authorization, including pairing tokens issued before the action.

trace.description: Accepts the native-registration request and verifies the signed native pairing token, including purpose and expiry.
Looks up and retains ownerID from the submitted old subscriberID before revocation can rotate that subscriber ID; no generation is captured for a later commit check.
The concurrent admin recovery path deletes the account's native devices before rotating the subscriber ID at lines 791-800, leaving registration and revocation as separate operations.
After the old owner was resolved, consumes the token nonce and upserts a new native device with a newly minted secret without rechecking subscriber generation or account liveness.

conditions.description: The attacker possesses an unexpired native pairing token and its subscriber ID, normally obtained from a QR/deep-link pairing flow.
Registration must resolve the old owner concurrently with an admin password reset, MFA clear, or deactivation before or during subscriber rotation.
For immediate access the account is active after MFA clear; after deactivation the persisted device becomes relevant if the account is later reactivated.

execution.attacker_perspective: A holder of a captured native pairing token whose account administrator is attempting to revoke devices or recover the account.
instructions: Obtain an unexpired native pairing token and subscriber ID before the administrator performs the recovery/revocation action.
Send native registration concurrently with the administrator's password reset, MFA clear, or deactivation request; arrange for registration to complete owner lookup before subscriber rotation.
Use a new valid device ID so registration does not require an existing-device secret.
Use the returned device secret to call a withMailAuth endpoint such as GET /api/inbox after MFA clear, or after reactivation if the account was deactivated.
execution.expected_result: The registration returns a device credential and a new native-device row remains after the administrator's purge. In the MFA-clear case the device can immediately access the account's mailbox.

remediation.strategy: Serialize subscriber-generation invalidation with native registration and credential deletion. Make registration conditional on the subscriber ID/generation still matching the value authorized at the start, and rotate/invalidate that generation before or within the same transaction as device deletion. Refuse registration when the generation changed or the account is no longer active.

code_changes.fixed_code: Re-read the current subscriber ID/generation under the same per-user/store lock immediately before UpsertNativeDevice and reject if it differs from the token's authorized generation.
Perform subscriber rotation and native-device deletion as one serialized revocation operation, so no registration can commit between the two steps.

likelihood.reason: The attacker needs a captured, still-valid pairing token and a narrow concurrent interleaving with an administrator's revocation action.

impact.reason: It defeats an explicit account-recovery revocation boundary and recreates a full paired-device mailbox credential; MFA clear leaves the recreated device immediately active.

confidence.reason: The registration and revocation order are directly visible in current source, the operations use separate lookup/store steps, and no subscriber-generation check or shared transaction exists before the new device is persisted.

reason: Mutable action tags in .github/workflows/release-image.yml violate the repository pinning contract and are documented as hardening, but no source-controlled attacker path was confirmed; exploitation requires compromise or retagging of an upstream action. This is not elevated to a confirmed vulnerability in this run.
